taxonomyNote: NatureServe follows Guyer et al. (2020), who redescribed N. beyeri and described the Apalachicola (N. moleri) and Escambia (N. mounti) lineages as new species; older sources (e.g. Outdoor Alabama) give a broader range to Georgia and Florida.
fieldMarks: Aquatic salamander 6.25-8.75 in long; dark brown ground colour with tan spots joining into a net-like pattern.
Some have a dark stripe through the eye; juveniles lighter with small dull yellow spots.
Four toes on all four feet.
behavior: Opportunistic feeder on fish, eggs, crayfish, mollusks and worms.
Courtship in fall and winter in other parts of the range; eggs laid April-June under debris on the bottom.
habitat: Sandy, spring-fed streams, also large rivers and standing backwater.
range: Gulf Coast drainages: western lineage from west-central Louisiana to northeastern and eastern Texas; other lineages from southeastern Louisiana to northeastern Mississippi and Alabama (Mobile Bay drainage).
